items.title: The Impact of Prolonged Pre-Heart Transplantation Left Ventricular Assist Device on Post-Transplantation Outcomes.
items.abstract: Durable mechanical circulatory support with a left ventricular assist device (LVAD) serves as bridge to heart transplantation (HTx) in patients with advanced heart failure. LVAD therapy is associated with improved outcomes, but has inherent limitations, including device-related complications. In this study, we aimed to evaluate the impact of prolonged LVAD support in patients who underwent HTx as compared to those without LVAD support. We retrospectively analysed 148 HTx recipients at University Medical Center Groningen, the Netherlands (2007-2023): 52 with prior LVAD support and 96 direct HTx patients. Outcomes included post-HTx survival, rejection requiring treatment, 1-year cardiac haemodynamics, and need for kidney replacement therapy. Median LVAD duration was 757 days (range 16-2,113). The LVAD group had fewer females (21% vs 54%; p 2 ; p=0.03) compared to direct HTx recipients. Prolonged LVAD support as bridge-to-transplantation showed no statistically significant differences with direct HTx in terms of post-HTx survival, rejection rates, and renal function despite minor differences in 1-year haemodynamic parameters.
authors: Stan A J van den Broek

items.title: Computed Tomography Coronary Angiography for Patients with Chest Pain: Ethnic Variation in Use, Coronary Atherosclerotic Burden, and Effect on Statin Treatment (ANZACS-QI 90).
items.abstract: We assessed ethnic differences in computed tomography coronary angiography (CTCA) utilisation, extent of coronary artery disease (CAD), and statin use among patients with chest pain at Middlemore Hospital, New Zealand. Patients without prior revascularisation (n=4,519) who underwent CTCA (2020-2024) were identified from the Aotearoa New Zealand Acute Coronary Syndrome Quality Improvement (ANZACS-QI) cardiac computed tomography registry. CTCA utilisation was assessed relative to incident acute coronary syndrome (ACS) hospitalisations in each age and ethnic group, which served as a surrogate for population CAD burden. CAD extent was assessed using the segment involvement score. Statin dispensing data were obtained from the national pharmaceutical data set. The cohort comprised 37.8% European/Other, 13.4% Māori, 19.8% Pacific, 15.5% Indian, and 13.5% other Asian patients. Māori, Pacific, and Indian patients (mean age, 55.7, 54.8, and 54.0 years, respectively) were younger than other Asian and European/Other patients (59.2 and 60.4 years, respectively; p<0.001). CTCA utilisation among those aged <55 years was lowest among Māori and Pacific patients, intermediate among European/Other and Indian patients, and highest among other Asian patients (CTCA-to-incident-ACS ratios, 2.5, 2.2, 3.0, 3.8, and 8.0, respectively). Indian and other Asian patients were most likely to have normal coronary arteries (p<0.001), while Māori and Pacific patients had the most extensive atherosclerosis (p<0.001). Post-CTCA statin use, for equivalent disease severity, was similar across ethnicities. Young Māori and Pacific patients with chest pain are underinvestigated and undertreated relative to their population CAD burden. However, when CAD is identified, statin treatment is equal across ethnic groups. Therefore, CTCA facilitates equitable treatment for Māori and Pacific patients presenting with chest pain.

Second-Line Treatment of ES-SCLC in the Immunotherapy Era: An Exploratory Real-World Study.
items.abstract: Currently, immunochemotherapy is the standard first-line treatment for extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC). However, all recommended second-line strategies have been investigated prior to the advent of immunotherapy, and real-world data on the subsequent treatment landscape in ES-SCLC after disease progression on first-line immunochemotherapy remain limited. To characterize the landscape and evaluate clinical outcomes of distinct second-line treatment regimens in patients with ES-SCLC who experienced disease progression following first-line immunochemotherapy in real-world practice. We retrospectively enrolled 94 patients with ES-SCLC who progressed after first-line immunochemotherapy and received second-line treatment between February 2020 and February 2024. Eligible patients were divided into three groups based on their second-line treatment regimens: the chemotherapy-alone (C) group, the immunochemotherapy (CI) group, and the anti-angiogenic-containing therapy (AT) group. Kaplan-Meier (K-M) method was applied to compare the survival outcomes. Multivariate Cox regression analyses were conducted to identify independent predictors. Further exploratory subgroup analyses stratified by platinum-free interval (PFI) were performed. The median progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) for all enrolled patients were 3.77 months and 9.80 months, respectively. Patients in the AT group exhibited the shortest PFS and OS compared to patients in the C group and CI group. Multivariate Cox proportional-hazards regression revealed that adrenal progression pattern was an independent adverse prognostic factor for PFS, whereas AT therapy was independently associated with worse OS. Exploratory subgroup analysis based on PFI showed no significant survival differences among the three treatment groups. For ES-SCLC patients progressing after first-line immunochemotherapy, second-line AT is associated with inferior OS, but this may reflect treatment selection bias rather than anti-angiogenic therapy itself. Moreover, regardless of PFI status, no significant differences in survival outcomes were observed among patients receiving different treatment regimens; thus, clinical trials should be recommended for patients receiving second-line therapy.

items.title: Macrophage Extracellular Vesicle-Camouflaged Framework Nucleic Acid Nanospheres Reprogram Lactate Metabolism-Immune Feedback Loops for Synergistic Chemoimmunotherapy of Glioblastoma.
items.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) and blood-brain tumor barrier (BBTB) severely limited drug delivery into the brain, while aberrant aerobic glycolysis in the tumor microenvironment caused excessive lactate accumulation and drove immunosuppression. These factors together constituted the core obstacles to glioblastoma (GBM) therapy. From the perspective of metabolism-immune crosstalk, we engineered a brain‑targeted nucleic acid nanosphere (TE@siP‑DNS/DOX) featuring high BBB/BBTB penetrability, which orchestrated a "triple‑linked" strategy integrating glycolysis blockade, immune microenvironment remodeling, and synergistic therapeutic potentiation. The nanosphere was constructed with a self‑assembled core of PKM2‑targeting siRNA and framework nucleic acids loaded with doxorubicin (DOX), shielded by a biomimetic shell of T7 peptide‑modified macrophage extracellular vesicles. Leveraging transcytosis and T7‑mediated active targeting, TE@siP‑DNS/DOX efficiently traversed the barriers and preferentially accumulated at tumor sites. DOX simultaneously provoked chemotherapy and immunogenic cell death, igniting robust CD8⁺ T cell‑mediated antitumor immunity, whereas siRNA‑mediated PKM2 silencing curtailed glycolysis, lessened lactate production, rewired metabolic circuitry, and forced macrophage polarization toward the M1 antitumor phenotype, thereby dismantling the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (iTME). Transcriptomic analysis further confirmed that metabolic and immune-related pathways were significantly enriched following TE@siP-DNS/DOX treatment, providing transcriptional evidence for its dual modulation of the metabolic-immune feedback loop. In vivo studies substantiated that TE@siP‑DNS/DOX markedly inhibited tumor growth and prolonged survival in orthotopic GBM-bearing mice. Collectively, this nanoplatform, through a synergistic feedback loop integrating metabolic regulation and immune activation, provides a good therapeutic strategy and research paradigm for enhanced glioma therapy. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Glioblastoma therapy is impeded by a multifaceted barrier system encompassing the blood-brain barrier, metabolic dysregulation, lactate accumulation, and immunosuppression. Here, we engineered a brain-targeted nucleic acid nanosphere that integrates glycolysis blockade, immune remodeling, and chemotherapeutic sensitization via a single platform. By combining PKM2 silencing with doxorubicin-loaded framework nucleic acids and T7-modified macrophage vesicles, the nanosphere achieves efficient barrier penetration, lactate reduction, M1 macrophage repolarization, and immunogenic cell death. This metabolism-immune feedback loop synergistically suppresses orthotopic tumors and extends survival. Our study provides a paradigm for treating brain tumors through concurrent metabolic reprogramming and antitumor immunity, offering a translatable strategy for overcoming therapy resistance in glioblastoma.

items.title: Cannabinoid receptor 2 promotes differentiation of T regulatory cells during allergic inflammation.
items.abstract: Allergic diseases remain a major clinical challenge because current treatments, such as antihistamines and corticosteroids, provide only symptomatic relief without addressing the underlying immune dysregulation. Induction of regulatory T cells (Tregs) to generate allergen tolerance has recently emerged as a potential form of therapy. Similarly, investigating the mechanisms and medical potential of the endocannabinoid system has become more popular in recent years. In particular, the CB2 receptor, which is most abundant in peripheral tissues and immune cells, offers a potential target for immunomodulation. In this study, we examined expression patterns of CB2 in atopic and nonatopic donors and investigated the effects of CB2 ligands and CB2 deficiency on immune cells in vitro and in vivo. We observed significantly decreased CB2 expression on CD4+ T cells from atopic donors, with expression levels positively correlating with Treg abundance. Furthermore, CB2 agonists and antagonists altered immune cell migration and differentiation, effects that were absent in CB2 knockout mice. Blocking the CB2 receptor in human CD4+ T cells decreased endogenous TGF-β secretion and downregulated IL-10 mRNA expression. Our study provides new insights into the effects of CB2 on human naïve CD4+ T cells and warrants further investigation of CB2-targeting compounds as potential adjuvants for allergen-specific immunotherapy.

items.title: Context-dependent regulation of lipid homeostasis by miR-122: Molecular mechanisms, disease relevance, and therapeutic implications.
items.abstract: miR-122 is a liver-enriched microRNA that shapes systemic lipid homeostasis by coordinating hepatic de novo lipogenesis, oxidative disposal, intracellular storage, and lipoprotein export. Mechanistically, miR-122 intersects with energy-sensing pathways centered on AMPK, modulates lipogenesis through Sirtuin-LKB1/AMPK control, influences triglyceride handling via YY1-linked transcriptional programs, and engages noncoding RNA circuits that regulate autophagy. Furthermore, intracellular miR-122 regulates lipid peroxidation (ferroptosis) in a highly context-dependent manner: it buffers against oxidative injury in steatotic hepatocytes and ischemic tissue injuries, yet actively promotes ferroptosis by targeting SLC7A11 and GPX4 in hepatocellular carcinoma and autoimmune hepatitis. Meanwhile, extracellular vesicle (EV)-associated miR-122 mediates pathogenic inter-organ metabolic communication. Clinically, the progressive decline of hepatic miR-122 drives the transition from simple steatosis to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), positioning circulating miR-122 as a highly sensitive diagnostic biomarker. Short-term antagonism via locked nucleic acid (LNA)-based anti-miRs efficiently lowers circulating cholesterol, yet preclinical models suggest that prolonged suppression risks progressive hepatic inflammatory remodeling and steatofibrosis. Conversely, for advanced liver diseases characterized by miR-122 depletion, miR-122 replacement therapies show potential to restore metabolic resilience and suppress fibrogenesis. This review synthesizes current mechanistic evidence and highlights the development of miR-122-targeted nucleic acid drugs and the therapeutic exploitation of exosomal vectors, providing a translational scene for managing lipid-driven metabolic and hepatic disorders.

items.title: Hepatitis C care cascade in a university hospital: Gaps in HCV RNA testing and treatment initiation.
items.abstract: Evaluation of the hepatitis C virus (HCV) care cascade using real-world data helps identify gaps in HCV elimination strategies. This study assessed the HCV care cascade in a tertiary-care university hospital in Türkiye and investigated factors associated with confirmatory HCV RNA testing. All individuals who underwent anti-HCV testing between 2017 and 2020 were retrospectively evaluated, without age restrictions. The cascade stages included anti-HCV positivity, confirmatory HCV RNA testing, antiviral treatment initiation, and post-treatment virological assessment. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with confirmatory HCV RNA testing. Among 95,836 individuals tested, 690 (0.72%) were anti-HCV positive. Confirmatory HCV RNA testing was performed in 505 (73.2%), of whom 151 (29.9%) had detectable HCV RNA. Treatment was initiated in 96 (63.6%) of the 151 viremic patients. Post-treatment HCV RNA results were available for 78 of the 96 treated patients; 18 had no documented post-treatment assessment. In multivariable analysis, evaluation in internal medicine departments (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 5.62; 95% CI, 3.77-8.37; P < 0.001) and higher anti-HCV signal-to-cutoff levels (aOR, 1.08; 95% CI, 1.04-1.13; P < 0.001) were independently associated with confirmatory testing. Confirmatory HCV RNA testing was the major point of attrition in the care cascade, with substantial differences between internal medicine and surgical departments. Additional gaps occurred in treatment initiation and post-treatment assessment. Reflex testing and electronic alerts may warrant evaluation as potential strategies to improve continuity of care.

items.title: No recurrent severe immune-related hepatitis during PD-L1 therapy after PD-1-related hepatitis in advanced gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma: a case report.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors have improved outcomes in advanced gastric and gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinomas, but immune-related adverse events may limit subsequent treatment options. Evidence remains limited regarding PD-L1 inhibitor therapy after PD-1 inhibitor-related hepatitis and regarding later-line agents such as utidelone and liposomal irinotecan in advanced adenocarcinoma of the esophagogastric junction. A 66-year-old man with resected gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma received first-line postoperative tislelizumab plus nab-paclitaxel/carboplatin in May 2023, but developed grade 3 immune-related hepatitis, leading to immunotherapy discontinuation. After chemotherapy and radiotherapy, metastatic recurrence was identified in February 2025, with nodules anterior and superior to the pancreatic body. Second-line treatment with adebrelimab, capecitabine, and utidelone was initiated. Notably, despite prior tislelizumab-associated hepatitis, no recurrent immune-related hepatitis occurred during adebrelimab-based therapy. Repeat PET/CT in August 2025 showed partial response according to RECIST 1.1, with marked shrinkage of the pancreatic-adjacent lesions. After subsequent progression, third-line treatment with adebrelimab, liposomal irinotecan, and capecitabine was started in November 2025. Follow-up CT in March 2026 demonstrated radiographic shrinkage of the lesion near the pancreas. This case highlights the heterogeneity of hepatic toxicity among immune checkpoint inhibitors and suggests that adebrelimab rechallenge may be possible after recovery from tislelizumab-related hepatitis. It also suggests potential clinical activity of utidelone- and liposomal irinotecan-containing regimens in heavily treated advanced gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma.

items.title: Distinct cellular source and bulk immune correlates of HAVCR2 expression in seminoma.
items.abstract: HAVCR2 (T-cell immunoglobulin and mucin domain-containing protein 3; TIM-3) expression is associated with favorable prognosis in seminoma, but its underlying immune context remains unclear. We sought to distinguish the cellular source of HAVCR2 from the immune correlates of its interpatient bulk expression using bulk and single-cell transcriptomic datasets. In The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) seminoma discovery cohort (n = 64), we evaluated associations between HAVCR2 expression and eight predefined immune-compartment signatures, adjusting for overall immune infiltration using PTPRC (CD45) and the ESTIMATE algorithm. After adjustment, associations with T-cell-, cytotoxicity-, and checkpoint-related signatures were attenuated or lost, whereas macrophage-related signatures remained correlated with HAVCR2 expression; on mutual adjustment, the general macrophage rather than the M2-associated signature retained this association. In an independent bulk cohort (GSE3218, n = 13), the M2-associated signature remained associated with HAVCR2 after PTPRC adjustment, whereas the general macrophage association was directionally concordant but attenuated after adjustment. Single-cell RNA sequencing of a four-donor seminoma cohort (GSE228501) showed background-level HAVCR2 expression in tumor cells, while HAVCR2-positive cells were detected in macrophage, exhaustion-like CD8 T-cell, and proliferating T-cell compartments, with donor-level mean expression numerically higher in exhaustion-like CD8 T cells than in macrophages. Although HAVCR2 was expressed across multiple immune compartments at the single-cell level, interpatient bulk HAVCR2 expression was associated with a macrophage-related immune context beyond overall immune infiltration, whereas the specific macrophage phenotype remained unresolved. These findings inform the interpretation of bulk HAVCR2 as a biomarker, including its previously reported prognostic association, without implying a causal role for macrophages in clinical outcome.

items.title: Tracing Responses to a Syndemic: A Systematic Map of Substance Use, Mental and Sexual Health Interventions for Gay, Bisexual and Other Men Who Have Sex With Men in Southeast Asia.
items.abstract: In Southeast Asia, a triple syndemic of substance use, poor mental and sexual health is shaped by regional political, economic and sociocultural environments and disproportionately affects gay, bisexual and other men who have sex with men (GBMSM). Yet, most GBMSM implementation research, regionally and globally, focuses narrowly on HIV prevention and care, with little attention to mental health and substance use. This review aimed to systematically map interventions addressing these interlinked areas of GBMSM wellbeing in Southeast Asia, identify evidence gaps and inform the design of holistic, syndemic-responsive interventions. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, we searched six databases (01/2010-06/2024) for intervention/evaluation studies including GBMSM (cis and trans) in Southeast Asia, reporting outcomes on substance use, mental and/or sexual health. We completed citation/full text screening and data extraction in duplicate. We mapped interventions by type and availability of outcome data. We identified 2016 unique records; 142 publications reported 130 studies describing 148 interventions reaching 154,502 GBMSM. Interventions focused primarily on sexual health (n = 143), concentrated along the care continuum. This included facility-based HIV testing (n = 25), community-based HIV testing (n = 14), HIV self-testing (n = 13), assisted partner notification (n = 1), pre-exposure prophylaxis (n = 29), post-exposure prophylaxis (n = 3), HIV treatment (n = 20), sexually transmitted infection/hepatitis C virus testing/treatment (n = 12) and vaccination (n = 2). Fewer interventions were behavioural and psychosocial, including psychosocial support (n = 7), education (n = 11) and outreach (n = 3). Three took miscellaneous approaches. Few interventions primarily focused on mental health and substance use. Three addressed mental health: two using psychosocial strategies, one of which had a dual sexual health focus, and one assessing depression following HIV treatment initiation. Two addressed substance use, both with psychosocial approaches. Mental health outcome data (primary/secondary) were presented in nine interventions; substance use in five, mostly as secondary measures. Only one intervention reported outcomes spanning all three syndemic domains. These findings reflect a narrow intervention landscape, shaped partly by funder priorities, that fails to fully address the intersecting challenges GBMSM face with substance use, mental and sexual health. In the rebuilding period following the closure of USAID and many US NIH-funded research initiatives, intervention development should take a broader view, crafting holistic services ameliorating multiple challenges. These must attend to local priorities and take account of regional contexts exacerbating the syndemic.

items.title: Copper (II) complexes involving quinazolinone Schiff base ligands: In vitro study of cytotoxic, genotoxic and DNA-protective potential in human hepatoma HepG2 cell line.
items.abstract: DNA oxidation damage contributes to carcinogenesis and limits the efficacy of many chemotherapeutics. Although platinum‑based drugs remain crucial in cancer therapy, their clinical use is restricted by toxicity and acquired resistance. However, quinazolinone derivatives have recently attracted attention as scaffolds with promising biological activities. Among these, Schiff bases are of particular interest because they can provide suitable ligands for the complexation with metals, making them a potential substitute for cisplatin. Therefore, in the search for new anticancer agents, Cu(II) complexes based on 2,3-substituted quinazolinones have been studied in detail. The radical scavenging/reducing efficiency and DNA-protective effects were monitored using DPPH, FRAP and DNA topology assays. Ligands and Cu(II) complexes, were screened for their in vitro cytotoxic, genotoxic, and protective activity in human hepatocarcinoma (HepG2) cells using the MTT and Comet assays. The results showed that compounds studied are redox-active agents. Cu(II) complexes exhibited higher DPPH radical-scavenging activity in comparison with their corresponding free ligands; they manifested comparable effects in ferric reducing power as well as in DNA topology assays. The cellular assays revealed markedly higher cytotoxicity of Cu(II) complexes compared with the corresponding free ligands. In the presence of H₂O₂, C1 significantly enhanced DNA damage, whereas C2 did not alter the level of DNA damage induced by H₂O₂ alone. On the contrary, ligands exhibited much lower toxicity and significant protection of HepG2 cells against H 2 O 2 . The incorporation of Cu(II) ions into quinazolinone Schiff base ligands substantially alters their biological activity, shifting their profile from DNA‑protective to cytotoxic/pro‑oxidant. DFT calculations were performed for both Cu(II) complexes to investigate molecular features that may contribute to their different biological activity. These results highlight the potential of quinazolinone‑Cu(II) complexes as anticancer candidates and support further studies into their mechanisms of action.

Comparison of pegfilgrastim and daily G-CSF for CD34 + cell mobilization in healthy donors and post-transplant engraftment: The Pegfilgrastim-23 Study.
items.abstract: Pegfilgrastim (Peg-G), a long-acting formulation of granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF), enables single-dose administration and effectively mobilizes CD34 + cells into the peripheral blood of healthy donors undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. However, prospective comparisons with conventional daily G-CSF (Daily-G) regarding mobilization efficacy and safety remain limited. Moreover, no previous studies have compared the differentiation profiles of CD34 + cells mobilized by these two agents. In this multicenter, prospective observational study, we assessed the efficacy, kinetics, safety and differentiation profiles of mobilized CD34 + cells induced by either 7.2 mg dose of Peg-G on day 1 (n = 29) or Daily-G at 400 μg/m 2 /day from day 1 (n = 31) in 60 healthy related donors scheduled to undergo CD34 + cell collection. Hematopoietic engraftment was also evaluated in 60 recipients following infusion of the collected peripheral blood stem cells. Of the 60 enrolled donors, 50 were evaluable for peripheral blood CD34 + cell counts. The mean CD34 + cell counts were 85.6 ± 48.0 × 10⁶/L in the Peg-G group and 84.6 ± 42.4 × 10⁶/L in the Daily-G group, with no significant difference between the groups (P = .992). Similar findings were observed in the analyses stratified by collection on days 4 and day 5. No significant differences were observed in the differentiation profiles of mobilized CD34⁺ cells. The kinetics of peripheral blood cell counts were generally comparable between the groups in both the day 4 and day 5 collection cohorts, except for a higher white blood cell count on day 4 in the Peg-G group among donors collected on day 5. In exploratory analyses, CD34⁺ cell mobilization efficacy was not correlated with day 4 serum G-CSF concentrations, donor age, body weight, body mass index, or body surface area in either of the treatment groups. Adverse events were common but predominantly consisted of pain-related symptoms that were manageable with supportive care. Grade 3 adverse events included liver dysfunction in three donors and hypertension in one. All laboratory abnormalities and clinical symptoms resolved by the follow-up assessment, and no grade ≥4 adverse events were observed in any donor. Median times to neutrophil engraftment were 16 and 15 days in the Peg-G and Daily-G groups, respectively (P = .73), and those to platelet engraftment were 30 and 27 days, respectively (P = .68). Single-dose 7.2-mg Peg-G and conventional Daily-G resulted in comparable peripheral blood CD34⁺ cell mobilization and differentiation profiles of mobilized CD34⁺ cells in healthy related donors, with generally manageable safety profiles. No significant differences in the time to neutrophil or platelet engraftment were observed between recipients in the two groups. These findings suggest that both mobilization strategies are clinically applicable and that regimen selection may be tailored according to drug-specific characteristics and donor convenience.

items.title: Histotripsy for Liver Malignancies: A Systematic Review of the Existing Literature.
items.abstract: Histotripsy is an emerging noninvasive, nonthermal ablative therapy recently introduced for the treatment of hepatic malignancies. This systematic review evaluated the efficacy and safety of histotripsy for primary and secondary liver tumors. PubMed and Scopus were searched from inception through August 2026 in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Search terms included combinations of subject headings and keywords such as "histotripsy," "hepatic," and "metastases." Ten clinical studies published between 2022 and 2026 met inclusion criteria. Study populations included hepatocellular carcinoma and metastases from colorectal, neuroendocrine, pancreatic, breast, and other malignancies. Technical success ranged from 68.8% to 100%, although definitions varied across studies. Early treatment efficacy and local control were generally high among successfully treated tumors, with several studies reporting rates exceeding 90%. Longer-term oncologic data were limited by heterogeneous imaging criteria, treatment intent, and patient populations. Major complications were uncommon, although vascular thrombosis and acute kidney injury emerged as potential safety concerns. Current evidence supports the technical feasibility and short-term efficacy of hepatic histotripsy. However, standardized outcome definitions, longer follow-up, and comparative studies are needed to establish its durability and role relative to existing liver-directed therapies.
